newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crude grades firm in spotty May business.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crude grades firm in spotty May business.

text.p: U.S. crude prices firmed Wednesday morning in thin volumes for May barrels ahead of pipeline scheduling day on Friday.

Traders said dealings would be spotty through the Friday deadline. Outright barrels gained slightly on mildly supportive inventory data released late Tuesday and earlier today. Potentially explosive tribal fighting in Nigerian oil regions also aided the June NYMEX contract.
Cash May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing remained even with June at $19.65-75 a barrel, 10 cents higher than late Tuesday. Traders pegged the May/June roll at flat.

Trades for domestic barrels featured strengthening Louisiana grades, with Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James turning around late Tuesday deficits to sell at flat. Current talk put LLS/St. James at steady to plus 10 cts versus WTI/Cushing.
West Texas Sour/Midland moved in tighter to the marker, too, getting sold at a $1.45 discount to WTI/Cushing. Traders said trading volumes were extremely thin and choppy.
May Postings Plus barrels were steady at $1.75, with the Louisiana swamp grades talked lightly.
Markets were focused on the probable delivery of Nigerian Bonny Light and North Sea Brent into the U.S. Gulf pipeline system against NYMEX for May.
May crudes were treated with some uncertainty with talk of foreign crudes coming into pipelines, an unusual happening, traders noted.
